newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi islamic Bank to offer 61 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi islamic Bank to offer 61 mln shares.

text.p: The newly-formed Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank plans to open subscription to 61 million shares on June 21 at 10 dirhams a share, a founding committee member was on Tuesday quoted as saying.
Abu Dhabi, one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), in May announced the setting up of the one billion dirham bank, which bankers said was the biggest Islamic bank in the world.

It said the Abu Dhabi government would own a 100 million dirham stake, the UAE president's private office would have 50 million dirhams and the founders -- who were not named -- 240 million dirhams. The rest would be offered to UAE nationals.
Khalifa al-Kindi, chairman of the bank's founding committee, was quoted by UAE newspapers as saying the bank will offer 61 million shares of 10 dirhams each from June 21.
He said the offer would be open for 20 days.

"It is proposed that the bank will retain net profits for the first three years for accumulating reserves as well as for good credit rating," he said. Profits from the year 2001 will be available for distribution to shareholders, he said.

He said the Islamic banking sector was growing in the Gulf Arab region. "The latest market statistics indicate that the available liquidity in the region to invest capital which agrees with Islamic sharia rules, is estimated at 400 million dirhams."
Islamic banks do not deal in interest -- the core of the Western banking system -- as it is regarded by many Moslems as usury, banned under Islamic sharia law.

Islamic banks have become more popular among the world's one billion Moslems, but the more than 185 financial institutions which strictly adhere to the principles of sharia law faced hurdles to lure more funds, bankers say.
